newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall by lunch on economic concern.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall by lunch on economic concern.

text.p: Thai stocks retreated by lunch after concern over the economy wiped out early gains spurred by expected March export recovery, analysts said on Tuesday.
The SET Index fell 4.91 points, or 0.74 percent, to 655.19 by the break. The SET 50 shed 0.23 points or 0.47 percent to 48.49 on modest 1.07 billion baht turnover.
"There doesn't seem to be much positive news in the market. Looking at the full year, there is still concern that exports may not meet targets," said an analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.

The early rally, pushing the index up to 663.03 shortly after opening, was fuelled by announcement last week by customs department officials that March exports rose to about 133 billion baht from 113 billion in February.

The department's figures normally differ from the Bank of Thailand's official statistics. The commerce ministry has set a 10 percent export growth target for 1997. Exports contracted marginally in 1996.
Sluggish economic growth prospects and likelihood of more depressing first quarter corporate earnings also dampened sentiment in late morning, traders said.
Profit taking and fundamental weakness of troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce ended the bank's recent short rally, traders said.
The bank, peaking in the morning at 9.70 baht, took the break shedding 0.80 to 8.10.
Finance stocks lost 2.60 percent and banks 0.31 percent though Thai Farmers Bank gained one baht to 115 and Bangkok Bank added one to 173.
